## The one finding that matters

**The reports pipeline — the product's headline deliverable — is still a template generator.**

[reports.py:22-37](backend/app/api/v1/reports.py#L22-L37) builds `ReportService` with `MockAgentService()`, whose output is hardcoded prose and returns `citations=[]`, `citation_warning=True`, `degraded=True` ([agent_service_mock.py:40-45](backend/app/services/agent_service_mock.py#L40-L45)). Ownership stays intrinsic to ``projects.owner_id``; this table records the
*additional* members a project has been shared with, and their role. Resolving a
caller's effective role therefore consults both sources, which keeps existing
owner-only projects correct without a data backfill (see

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from sqlalchemy import DateTime, ForeignKey, Index, String, UniqueConstraint
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship

from app.db.models.base import Base, CreatedAtMixin, UUIDPrimaryKeyMixin

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from app.db.models.user import User


class ProjectRole(StrEnum):
    """Roles a caller can hold within one project (design §2.2).

    Ordered by capability: an owner may do everything an editor may, and an
    editor everything a viewer may. :attr:`rank` encodes that ordering so
    "at least this role" checks are a single comparison rather than a set
    membership test that has to be kept in sync by hand.
    """

    VIEWER = "viewer"
    EDITOR = "editor"
    OWNER = "owner"

    @property
    def rank(self) -> int:
        return _ROLE_RANK[self]

    def at_least(self, required: ProjectRole) -> bool:
        return self.rank >= required.rank


_ROLE_RANK: dict[ProjectRole, int] = {
    ProjectRole.VIEWER: 1,
    ProjectRole.EDITOR: 2,
    ProjectRole.OWNER: 3,
}


class ProjectMember(UUIDPrimaryKeyMixin, CreatedAtMixin, Base):
    """One user's membership of one project, with a role."""

    __tablename__ = "project_members"
    __table_args__ = (
        # A user holds at most one role per project.
        UniqueConstraint("project_id", "user_id", name="uq_project_members_project_user"),
        Index("ix_project_members_project_id", "project_id"),
        Index("ix_project_members_user_id", "user_id"),
    )

    project_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("projects.id", ondelete="CASCADE"),
        nullable=False,
    )
    user_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE"),
        nullable=False,
    )
    #: Stored as text for a readable audit trail; validated against
    #: :class:`ProjectRole` in the service layer.
    role: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20), nullable=False)

from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.db.models.project_member import ProjectMember


class ProjectMemberRepository:
    """Persistence for :class:`ProjectMember`, always scoped to a project."""

    def __init__(self, session: AsyncSession) -> None:
        self._session = session

    async def create(
        self,
        *,
        project_id: UUID,
        user_id: UUID,
        role: str,
        invited_by: UUID | None,
    ) -> ProjectMember:
        member = ProjectMember(
            project_id=project_id,
            user_id=user_id,
            role=role,
            invited_by=invited_by,
        )
        self._session.add(member)
        await self._session.flush()
        return member

    async def get_for_user(self, project_id: UUID, *, user_id: UUID) -> ProjectMember | None:
        """Return the caller's membership row, if any.

        The project *owner* has no row here by default — ownership is intrinsic
        to ``projects.owner_id`` — so a ``None`` result means "not an invited
        member", not "no access". Role resolution combines both sources.
        """
        statement = select(ProjectMember).where(
            ProjectMember.project_id == project_id,
            ProjectMember.user_id == user_id,
        )
        result = await self._session.execute(statement)
        return result.scalar_one_or_none()

    async def get_by_id(self, member_id: UUID, *, project_id: UUID) -> ProjectMember | None:
        statement = select(ProjectMember).where(
            ProjectMember.id == member_id,
            ProjectMember.project_id == project_id,
        )
        result = await self._session.execute(statement)
        return result.scalar_one_or_none()

    async def list_for_project(self, *, project_id: UUID) -> list[ProjectMember]:
        statement = (
            select(ProjectMember)
            .where(ProjectMember.project_id == project_id)
            .order_by(ProjectMember.invited_at)
        )
        result = await self._session.execute(statement)
        return list(result.scalars().all())

    async def delete(self, member: ProjectMember) -> None:
        await self._session.delete(member)
        await self._session.flush()

class ActivityRepository:

        self,

        project_id: UUID,

from app.db.models.notification import Notification


class NotificationRepository:
    """Persistence for per-user in-app notifications."""

        self._session = session

    async def create(
        self,
        *,
        user_id: UUID,
        type: str,
        title: str,
        message: str,
        project_id: UUID | None = None,
        link: str | None = None,

    async def list_for_user(self, *, user_id: UUID, limit: int = 20) -> list[Notification]:
        statement = (
            select(Notification)
            .where(Notification.user_id == user_id)
            .order_by(Notification.created_at.desc())
            .limit(limit)
        )
        result = await self._session.execute(statement)
        return list(result.scalars().all())

    async def count_unread(self, *, user_id: UUID) -> int:
        statement = (
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(Notification)
            .where(Notification.user_id == user_id, Notification.read.is_(False))
        )
        result = await self._session.execute(statement)
        return int(result.scalar_one())

    async def mark_read(self, notification_id: UUID, *, user_id: UUID) -> bool:
        """Mark one notification read, scoped to its owner.

        Returns ``False`` when no such notification belongs to ``user_id`` — the
        caller maps that to 404, so one user's notification ids are not
        probeable by another (design §9.3 rule 4).
        """

            update(Notification)
            .where(Notification.id == notification_id, Notification.user_id == user_id)
            .values(read=True)
        )
        result = await self._session.execute(statement)
        await self._session.flush()
        return bool(result.rowcount)

{"kind":"tool","id":"jPSDMNtCzaw","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"backend/app/services/membership_service.py","instructions":"Add the membership service with role resolution and invitation logic.","content":""""Project membership and role resolution (Phase 10, FR-H6, design §2.2).

Ownership remains intrinsic to ``projects.owner_id``; this service treats the
owner as an implicit, non-removable member and layers invited members on top.
That keeps owner-only projects correct with no data backfill, and gives callers
one place to ask "what may this user do here?".

Every method here is pure business logic: routers authorise by calling
:meth:`MembershipService.require`, and never inspect roles themselves.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime
from uuid import UUID

from app.core.errors import ConflictError, NotFoundError, PermissionDeniedError
from app.db.models.project import Project
from app.db.models.project_member import ProjectMember, ProjectRole
from app.db.repositories.project_member_repository import ProjectMemberRepository
from app.db.repositories.user_repository import UserRepository


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class MemberView:
    """One member of a project, owner included.

    ``id`` is the membership row's id, and is ``None`` for the owner, who has no
    row — the UI uses it as a key and disables mutating controls when it is
    absent or when the role is ``owner``.
    """

    id: UUID | None
    user_id: UUID
    em [… 3,505 characters omitted] ather than stored pending: the
        account must already exist, and the added user sees the project on their
        next dashboard load (Phase 10 acceptance criterion).

        Raises
        ------
        NotFoundError
            If no account exists for ``email``.
        ConflictError
            If the user already has access to the project.
        """
        if role is ProjectRole.OWNER:
            # Ownership is transferred, never granted by invitation — an
            # invitation must not create a second owner.
            raise ConflictError("A project has exactly one owner; invite an editor or viewer.")

        user = await self._users.get_by_email(email)
        if user is None:
            raise NotFoundError("No account exists with that email address.")

        if user.id == project.owner_id:
            raise ConflictError("That user already owns this project.")

        existing = await self._members.get_for_user(project.id, user_id=user.id)
        if existing is not None:
            raise ConflictError("That user is already a member of this project.")

        return await self._members.create(
            project_id=project.id,
            user_id=user.id,
            role=role.value,
            invited_by=inviter_id,
        )

    async def change_role(
        self, project: Project, *, member_id: UUID, role: ProjectRole
    ) -> ProjectMember:
        """Change an invited member's role.

        The owner has no membership row, so an owner target is naturally a 404 —
        ownership is never editable through this path.
        """
        if role is ProjectRole.OWNER:
            raise ConflictError("Ownership cannot be granted through a role change.")

        member = await self._members.get_by_id(member_id, project_id=project.id)
        if member is None:
            raise NotFoundError("Member not found.")

        member.role = role.value
        return member

    async def remove_member(self, project: Project, *, member_id: UUID) -> None:
        """Remove an invited member. The owner cannot be removed."""
        member = await self._members.get_by_id(member_id, project_id=project.id)
        if member is None:
            raise NotFoundError("Member not found.")
        await self._members.delete(member)

to learn it finished. Notifications are per-user and optional-link: everything
else about the artifact stays in ``reports``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID

from app.db.models.notification import Notification, NotificationType
from app.db.repositories.notification_repository import NotificationRepository


class NotificationService:
    """Create and read per-user in-app notifications."""

    def __init__(self, *, notification_repository: NotificationRepository) -> None:
        self._notifications = notification_repository

    async def notify(
        self,
        *,
        user_id: UUID,
        title: str,
        message: str,
        type: str,
        project_id: UUID | None = None,
        link: str | None = None,
    ) -> Notification:
        return await self._notifications.create(
            user_id=user_id,
            type=type,
            title=title,
            message=message,
            project_id=project_id,
            link=link,
        )

    async def notify_report_completed(
        self,
        *,
        user_id: UUID,
        project_id: UUID,
        report_title: str,
        succeeded: bool,
    ) -> Notification:
        """Tell the requesting user their artifact finished (or failed)."""
        if succeeded:
            return await self.notify(
                user_id=user_id,
                project_id=project_id,
                type=NotificationType.REPORT_COMPLETED,
                title="Report ready",
                message=f"“{report_title}” finished generating.",
                link=f"/projects/{project_id}/reports",
            )
        return await self.notify(
            user_id=user_id,
            project_id=project_id,
            type=NotificationType.REPORT_COMPLETED,
            title="Report failed",
            message=f"“{report_title}” could not be generated.",
            link=f"/projects/{project_id}/reports",
        )

    async def list_for_user(self, *, user_id: UUID, limit: int = 20) -> list[Notification]:
        return await self._notifications.list_for_user(user_id=user_id, limit=limit)

    async def unread_count(self, *, user_id: UUID) -> int:
        return await self._notifications.count_unread(user_id=user_id)

    async def mark_read(self, notification_id: UUID, *, user_id: UUID) -> None:
        """Mark one notification read, raising 404 for a foreign or missing id."""
        from app.core.errors import NotFoundError

        marked = await self._notifications.mark_read(notification_id, user_id=user_id)
        if not marked:
            raise NotFoundError("Notification not found.")

Derived entirely from ``agent_traces``, which every agent invocation has been
writing since Phase 5 — no new instrumentation, and no second source of truth
that could drift from the Reasoning Trace panel.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from uuid import UUID

from app.db.repositories.agent_trace_repository import AgentTraceRepository


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AgentUsage:
    """One agent's share of a project's spend."""

    agent_name: str
    trace_count: int
    tokens_used: int
    estimated_cost: float


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class UsageSummary:
    """A project's total spend plus its per-agent breakdown."""

    run_count: int
    trace_count: int
    tokens_used: int
    estimated_cost: float
    by_agent: list[AgentUsage]


class UsageService:
    """Aggregate a project's recorded agent activity."""

    def __init__(self, *, trace_repository: AgentTraceRepository) -> None:
        self._traces = trace_repository

    async def summary(self, *, project_id: UUID) -> UsageSummary:
        runs, traces, tokens, cost = await self._traces.summarize_for_project(
            project_id=project_id
        )
        by_agent = [
            AgentUsage(
                agent_name=agent_name,
                trace_count=trace_count,
                tokens_used=agent_tokens,
                estimated_cost=agent_cost,
            )
            for agent_name, trace_count, agent_tokens, agent_cost in (
                await self._traces.usage_by_agent(project_id=project_id)
            )
        ]
        return UsageSummary(
            run_count=runs,
            trace_count=traces,
            tokens_used=tokens,
            estimated_cost=round(cost, 6),
            by_agent=by_agent,
        )

import { apiRequest } from '@/lib/api/client';
import type { ActivityEntry, Page, ProjectMember, ProjectRole, ProjectUsage } from '@/types/api';

export async function listMembers(token: string, projectId: string): Promise<ProjectMember[]> {
  return apiRequest<ProjectMember[]>(`/projects/${projectId}/members`, { token });
}

/**
 * Mutations return the refreshed roster, so the panel never has to reconcile a
 * single row against the list it already holds.
 */
export async function inviteMember(
  token: string,
  projectId: string,
  payload: { email: string; role: Exclude<ProjectRole, 'owner'> },
): Promise<ProjectMember[]> {
  return apiRequest<ProjectMember[]>(`/projects/${projectId}/members`, {
    method: 'POST',
    body: payload,
    token,
  });
}

export async function updateMemberRole(
  token: string,
  projectId: string,
  memberId: string,
  role: Exclude<ProjectRole, 'owner'>,
): Promise<ProjectMember[]> {
  return apiRequest<ProjectMember[]>(`/projects/${projectId}/members/${memberId}`, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    body: { role },
    token,
  });
}

export async function removeMember(
  token: string,
  projectId: string,
  memberId: string,
): Promise<ProjectMember[]> {
  return apiRequest<ProjectMember[]>(`/projects/${projectId}/members/${memberId}`, {
    method: 'DELETE',
    token,
  });
}

export async function listActivity(
  token: string,
  projectId: string,
  params: { page?: number; pageSize?: number } = {},
): Promise<Page<ActivityEntry>> {
  const query = new URLSearchParams();
  if (params.page) query.set('page', String(params.page));
  if (params.pageSize) query.set('page_size', String(params.pageSize));
  const suffix = query.toString() ? `?${query.toString()}` : '';

  return apiRequest<Page<ActivityEntry>>(`/projects/${projectId}/activity${suffix}`, { token });
}

export async function getUsage(token: string, projectId: string): Promise<ProjectUsage> {
  return apiRequest<ProjectUsage>(`/projects/${projectId}/usage`, { token });
}
